From all the buddhas, he attains all the superknowledges of a buddha and the unshakable liberation of mind.
This is called the restraint of the mind.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Listen all with undistracted minds as I speak of the restraint of the mind.
Having heard it, practice it accordingly if you desire swift purification."
By means of restraint of the mind, the wise obtain that which is supremely peaceful, vast, and immovable;
they contemplate the marvelous nature of the Jina’s Dharma—this is called the pure restraint of the mind.
By means of which restraint of the mind the wise one attains the constant, unshakable liberation of the mind,
as well as the supreme concentration like a diamond— this is indeed called the most excellent restraint of the mind.
Furthermore, by means of which the wise one accomplishes the ray of light of skillful means that brings about vast benefit,
and by means of which one obtains a voice endowed with the eight noble qualities— this is called the pure restraint of the mind.

By means of restraint of the mind, the wise one quickly attains the excellent thirty-two marks, as well as the powers and all the qualities of a Buddha; therefore, this restraint of the mind is declared to be supreme.
By means of restraint of the mind, the wise obtain the analytical knowledges as well as fearlessness;
likewise, they attain supreme, wondrous, and inconceivable qualities—thus has this excellent restraint of the mind been described.
By means of restraint of the mind, the wise one attains the four foundations of mindfulness and the bases of psychic power,
as well as the right efforts, the powers, and the faculties; this restraint of the mind is declared to be supreme.

By means of this swift restraint of the mind, the wise person attains the seven stainless factors of enlightenment, as well as the excellent eightfold path; thus is this restraint of the mind declared to be supreme.

By means of restraint of the mind, the wise attain the supreme dwelling in great equanimity and the stainless, supreme dwelling in compassion; this restraint of the mind is declared to be the most excellent.
By means of restraint of the mind, the wise one always attains auspicious and secure pure thoughts;
he becomes rich in virtues through discourse on seclusion—this is declared to be the supreme restraint of the mind.
The wise one who is endowed with restraint of the mind does not dwell with false or evil views;
he generates neither malice nor covetousness—this is declared to be the supreme restraint of the mind.

The wise one who is endowed with restraint of the mind does not practice hypocrisy even for a moment, nor does he produce deceit toward his teachers; this is declared to be the supreme restraint of the mind.
The wise one who is endowed with restraint of the mind does not give rise to passion or hatred;
likewise, he never gives rise to a deluded mind. This is declared to be the supreme restraint of the mind.

The wise one who is endowed with restraint of the mind does not let the thought of awakening depart, nor does he disturb his resolute intention; this is declared to be the supreme restraint of the mind.
The wise one who is endowed with this restraint of the mind does not dwell together with any other various faults of the mind; this restraint of the mind is said to be supreme. (SRS 38.86)
The mind enters into the likeness of an illusion, and likewise the likeness of a dream or a mirage;
it has the characteristic of a reflection—this is always taught as the supreme restraint of the mind.
He enters into pleasure as being like a dream, likewise as impermanent, empty, and non-eternal;
it is the mind itself that he enters, by which the wise one is said to possess this supreme restraint of the mind.
One enters into the state where there is no life-principle and no sentient being; the mind arises from conditions like a wheel.
It has come from nowhere, nor has it gone anywhere—this is taught as the supreme restraint of the mind.
He does not conceive of that anywhere, nor does he imagine it, nor does he think of it;
he does not grasp at it, nor does he settle upon it—this is taught as the supreme restraint of the mind.
One penetrates ultimate truth as being like a dream, and one penetrates nirvāṇa as being like a dream;
when the mind penetrates in this way, the wise one is said to have attained this supreme restraint of the mind.
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter of the *Śrīsamādhirāja*, titled "The Chapter on the Restraint of Body, Speech, and Mind."
(Vaidya 296) Chapter 39: The Exposition of the Three Hundred Stanzas on the Feet.
In this regard, young man, what is the purification of karma?
That is to say, having seen the three realms of existence as being like a dream, one generates detachment toward them;
this is called the purification of karma.

In that regard, what is the transcendence of objects? It is this: perceiving the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields as being like an illusion, and the relinquishing of them—this is called the transcendence of objects.
In that regard, what is the full comprehension of the aggregates? It is this: entering into the realization that the aggregates are like a mirage.
In that regard, what is the equality of the elements?
It is the relinquishing of the elements which are like magical emanations.
In that regard, what is the non-excellence of the sense bases?
It is the relinquishing of those sense bases that are like reflections.
— What is the abandonment of craving?
It is the non-apprehension of all phenomena.
— — — What is the direct realization of non-arising?
It is the non-apprehension of all phenomena.
— What is the entrance into action?
It is the elimination of suffering that has arisen from diligence.
— — — What is the illumination of the cause?
It is the manifestation of the aggregates, which are like an echo.
— — What is the non-perishing of the fruit?
It is this: the non-perishing of the fruit of karma, which is like a dream.
— What is the vision of phenomena?
It is this: the non-seeing of all phenomena.
— — — What is the cultivation of the path?
It is this: the cultivation of the non-apprehension of all phenomena.
— What is meeting with the Tathāgatas?
It is this: the practice of the training of all Buddhas.
— What is sharp wisdom?
It is the patient acceptance of the non-arising of all phenomena.
What is the knowledge of entering into sentient beings?
It is the knowledge that discerns the superior and inferior faculties [of sentient beings].
In that regard, what is the knowledge of phenomena (dharmajñāna)?
It is this: the non-apprehension of all phenomena.
What is the knowledge of entering into the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*)?
It is this: the entry into the method of phenomena as they truly are.
— — — What is the knowledge of the differentiation of syllables?
It is this: the knowledge of the application of the three mantras, and the knowledge of forms and formlessness.
— What is the transcendence of entities?
It is the realization that there are no entities.
— What is the thorough knowledge of sound? It is the knowledge of entering [into the nature of] sounds as being like an echo.
— — What is the attainment of joy?
It is this: the non-apprehension of all phenomena, which is the relinquishing and the removal of the suffering of cyclic existence.
— What is the experience of joy in the Dharma? It is this: being content with instruction and seeing the benefits of not relinquishing it.
— What is uprightness? It is the penetration of the noble truths.
— Straightness? It is this: the non-distortion of one’s deportment.
— What is being free from frowning?
It is this: the abandonment of hatred.
— — What is good conduct (*sauśīlya*)? It is this: being pleasant to dwell with (*sukhasaṃvāsa*).
— What is sweetness?
It is this: being a source of beneficial things for others.
— What is meant by "having been previously invited"?
It is this: [the donor] says the words "Come, welcome," and [the recipient] rises quickly.
— — What is reverence for the guru? It is this: having both a sense of awe toward the gurus and regarding them as spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
— — What is service to the guru? It is this: attending upon, rising for, and serving the gurus.
What is contentment with rebirth? It is the lack of delight in any form of rebirth. What is satiety regarding wholesome qualities?
That is to say: the pursuit of pure dharmas and the seeking of what is wholesome.
In that regard, what is purity of livelihood? It is this: contentment with whatever one receives, absence of hypocrisy, absence of scheming, and not seeking gain through gain.
— What is the non-abandonment of dwelling in the forest?
It is this: not casting off the burden regarding wholesome qualities;
delighting in remote lodgings and seats; finding joy in forests, thickets, mountain fastnesses, caves, and ravines; and experiencing the joy of the Dharma.
Non-association with householders and renunciants, lack of attachment to honor and fame, and the experience of the joy of meditation through the abandonment of craving—
this is called the non-abandonment of dwelling in the forest.
In that regard, what is the knowledge of the establishment of the stages?

It is this: the knowledge of the establishment of the fruits of the stage of the śrāvaka, the knowledge of the establishment of the stage of the pratyekabuddha, and the knowledge of the establishment of the stage of the bodhisattva.
In that regard, what is the non-forgetfulness of mindfulness?
That is to say: mental attention directed toward impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self.
In that regard, what is the knowledge of skillfulness concerning the aggregates?
It is the knowledge of the distinctions among the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, as well as the non-apprehension of them therein.
In that regard, what is the direct realization of the superknowledges?
It is the attainment of the four bases of psychic power and the exercise of miraculous transformations.
In that regard, what is the removal of afflictions?
It is the abandonment of passion, hatred, and delusion.
In that regard, what is the knowledge of uprooting the continuity of latent predispositions?
It is the loathing of former childish conduct and the lack of longing for the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
In that regard, what is the state of progressing toward excellence? It is the accomplishment of the Buddha’s fearlessnesses and analytical knowledges.
In that regard, what is the outflow of cultivation?
It is this: the abandonment of attachment and aversion.
In that regard, what is skillfulness concerning transgressions?
It is this: the restraint of the Prātimokṣa and the Vinaya.
— What is the suppression of the outbursts of defilements?
It is the confession of transgressions and the restraint against unwholesome states in the future.
— — — — What is the abandonment of attachment?

It is this: the uprooting of the creeper of craving for existence within the three realms; the non-arising of unwholesome states that have not yet arisen; and the non-destruction of wholesome roots that have already arisen.
— What is the transcendence of existence?
It is this: the non-apprehension of the triple world and the state of non-mental engagement.
— What is the recollection of past births?
It is this: the knowledge of former abodes.
What is freedom from doubt regarding the ripening of karma?
It is the avoidance of the views of annihilationism and eternalism.
In that regard, what is reflection on the Dharma?
It is this: reflection on things as they truly are.
In that regard, what is the seeking of the teachings?
It is the upholding and cultivation of the Śrāvaka and Pratyekabuddha Piṭakas as well as the Bodhisattva Piṭaka.
What is the sharpness of knowledge?
It is the knowledge of non-arising which is like a dream.
What is thirst for knowledge?
It is the seeking of knowledge.
— What is the realization of knowledge?
It is the accomplishment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. — What is the stage of the well-bred horse?
That is to say, this is the locus of training for a bodhisattva.
— What is being like a mountain? It is this: not relinquishing the thought of awakening (bodhicitta). — What is immovability?
That is to say, being unassailable by the afflictions.
— What is immovability? It is this: non-attention toward all signs.
— — What is the characteristic of irreversibility?
It is this: the non-deficiency of the six perfections and the constant vision of the Buddhas residing in other world-systems.
— What is the perfection of wholesome qualities?
It is this: being in close proximity to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
What is the loathing of evil deeds?
It is this: restraint for the future and the non-arising of evil.
What is the non-occurrence of the afflictions?
It is this: the non-arising of ignorance, the craving for existence, and anger.
What is the non-abandonment of the training?
It is this: conviction in the ripening of karma and reverence for the Buddha.
— — — What is the establishment of meditative concentration (*samādhi*)?
It is skill in the non-arising and non-perishing of the mind and mental factors, as well as one-pointedness of mind.
What is the knowledge of the inclinations of sentient beings?
It is the knowledge that discerns the superior and inferior faculties [of beings].
— What is the knowledge of the distinctions among rebirths?
It is the knowledge of the established order of the five destinies.
What is the infinity of knowledge?
It is the effortless knowledge regarding mundane and supramundane arts and crafts.
What is the knowledge of the connection of speech?
It is the thorough understanding of the intentional terminology spoken by the Tathāgata.
— What is the renunciation of dwelling in a household? It is this: the departure characterized by seclusion of body and mind.
— What is non-attachment to the three realms? It is the vision of the three realms as they truly are.
What is the non-depression of the mind?
It is the non-abandonment of the mind and the non-abandonment while entering meditative equipoise.
What is attachment to phenomena?
It is the abandonment of all affection.
— — What is the upholding of the Dharma? It is this: the protection of the enlightenment of the Buddhas and the receiving of these very sūtras.
— — — What is the protection of the Dharma?
It is the suppression, in accordance with the Dharma, of those who reject the true Dharma.
What is the state of fearing the ripening of karma?
It is this: refraining from evil deeds out of a sense of shame, and applying oneself with diligence to the pursuit of wholesome qualities.
— What is skill in the Vinaya? It is this: the understanding of transgressions and non-transgressions by their very nature.
— — — What is the pacification of legal disputes?
It is this: the avoidance of assemblies.
— What is non-contention and non-dispute?
It is this: the pointlessness of worldly talk.
— — — What is the stage of patience (*kṣāntibhūmi*)?
It is this: the endurance of physical and mental affliction.
— — — What is the undertaking of patience?
It is this: equanimity toward ill-spoken words from others and the non-fracturing of patience.
— What is the discernment of phenomena (*dharmapravicaya*)?
It is the differentiation of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, as well as the differentiation of the categories of affliction and purification, and the non-apprehension of them.
What is skill in the definitive discernment of phenomena?
It is the ineffability of all phenomena.
What is the knowledge that discerns the distinctions between the words of the Dharma?
It is the thorough determination and investigation of the established nature of all phenomena.
What is skill in the production of the words of the Dharma? It is the teaching of phenomena exactly as they are.
What is the knowledge of skill in bringing about the discernment of what is beneficial and what is harmful?
It is this: the non-removal and non-addition to the intrinsic nature of phenomena (*dharmaprakṛti*).
— What is knowledge of the past?
It is this: knowledge of causes.
— What is knowledge of the future limit?
It is this: knowledge of conditions.
— What is the knowledge of the purity of the three spheres?
It is the non-apprehension and the non-mental engagement of phenomena belonging to the past, future, and present.
— What is the abiding of the mind?
It is this: the non-apprehension of the mind.
— What is the establishment of the body?
It is this: mindfulness directed toward the body.
... What is the characteristic of deportment (*īryāpatha*)?
It is this state of being undeluded regarding the noble qualities (*āryadharma*).
... What is the non-disturbance of deportment?
That is to say, being virtuous in secret.
What is the non-conceptualization of postures?
It is this: being free from evil desires.
— What is the clarity of the sense faculties?
It is this: attention directed toward the Dharma, speaking appropriately, knowing the right time, and the true revelation of phenomena as they really are.
...What is knowledge of the world? It is this: not being consciously aware of transgressions.
...What is relinquishment through liberation?
It is this: the non-grasping of existing things and the absence of envy.
...What is the state of having outstretched hands?
It is this: the habit of sharing with others.
... What is the state of having an ungrasping mind?
It is this: the absence of turbidity in one's faith.
...What is modesty? It is the absence of loquacity.
...bowed down out of a sense of shame.
That is to say, the state of not being directed toward [it].
What is the loathing of unwholesome states of mind? It is the recognition of them as the qualities of fools and the avoidance of association with them.
What is the non-abandonment of the ascetic practices (*dhūta*)?
It is this: firmness in one's undertaking.
What is the state of being endowed with right conduct? It is the thorough understanding of the sequence of postures and movements.
What is the practice of joy?
It is the state of mind that perceives the benefits of wholesome qualities.
...What is rising from one's seat for the teachers? It is this: the absence of pride and the absence of indolence.
...What is the restraint of pride?
It is this: the non-apprehension of a self and its lack of objective support.
...What is the gathering of the mind?
It is the knowledge that white dharmas do not perish.
...What is the encouragement of the mind?
That is to say, it is the knowledge that the fruit of diligence is never lost.
What is the knowledge of the analytical discernment of meaning?
It is the knowledge of the penetration of the truths as they truly are.
...What is the realization of knowledge?
It is the thorough understanding of mundane and supramundane phenomena.
...What is the departure from ignorance?
It is the departure from the superimposition of things as they truly are.
... What is the knowledge of entering the mind?
It is this: the knowledge of arising and passing away.
What is the knowledge of skill in taking up and setting aside food?
It is this: the possession of sharp wisdom.
...What is the knowledge of sounds and cries?
It is this: the manifestation of phenomena exactly as they are.
...What is the knowledge of establishment?
It is this: the knowledge of entering into things as they truly are.
...What is the determination of meaning?
It is this: the cutting off of the aggregate of formations.
...What is the avoidance of what is beneficial and what is harmful?
It is this: the transcendence of existence for oneself, and the leading of others to the transcendence of existence.
...What is reliance upon holy persons?
It is this: not being separated from the Buddhas.
...What is association with superior persons?
It is this: the practice of serving Buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas.
...What is the avoidance of unworthy persons? It is this: the shunning of those who perceive things as real and those who are indolent.
...What is delight in meditation? It is this: the avoidance of the thorns of sensual desire and the non-abandonment of the meditative absorptions.
And by not abandoning joy.
What is non-attachment to the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*)?
It is the desire to transcend the three realms, the desire to bring sentient beings to maturity, and the desire for the illumination of higher wisdom.
...What is the mastery of miraculous transformations through the superknowledges?
It is this: abiding in the five superknowledges, the thorough proclamation of the Buddha-qualities that are difficult to understand for others.
...What is the conventional designation of names?
It is the thorough comprehension of names that are not ultimately established.
...What is conventional designation?
It is this: worldly convention.
...What is the eradication of designations?
It is this: the knowledge of verbal expression.
...What is the cessation of saṃsāra?
It is this: the contemplation of the defects of saṃsāra.
...What is the state of not desiring gain?
It is this: having truly few desires.
... What is the lack of acceptability regarding gain and honor?
It is this: freedom from longing and the absence of evil desires.
What is fearlessness in the face of disparagement?
It is the knowledge that results from the investigation of the aggregates and the elements.
What is the non-adherence to the colors of beings?
It is this: being one who conceals one's own virtues and perceiving gain and honor as obstacles.
What is equanimity toward honors?
It is the understanding that this is the ripening of karma.
What is the state of being undaunted by lack of hospitality?
It is this: not relinquishing one's yoga.
What is the state of not becoming angry when reviled?
It is this: the discernment of worldly phenomena.
...What is equanimity regarding praise?
It is this: the going forth for the sake of seeking virtuous qualities.
What is lack of dejection when there is no gain?
It is this: the reflective examination of phenomena produced by oneself. What is lack of intimacy with householders?
That is to say, the avoidance of all material things whatsoever.
What is non-association with those who have gone forth?
It is this: the avoidance of the unwholesome and the pursuit of the wholesome.
...What is the avoidance of improper spheres of activity?
It is the abandonment of the five hindrances.
... What is the range of activity?
It is this: the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness.
...What is the perfection of conduct?
It is this: guarding others.
What is the avoidance of improper conduct?
It is this: the protection of one's own wholesome qualities.
What is the non-defiling of families?
It is this: the avoidance of being a knower.
... What is the protection of the teaching?
It is this: the undertaking of the search for the Dharma and the practice of the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma.
What is being of few words?
It is the attainment of tranquility (śamatha).
...What is gentleness? It is the attainment of insight (vipaśyanā).
What is skill in replying? It is the knowledge of how to respond and counter-respond.
...What is the subduing of adversaries?
It is the illumination and the establishment of phenomena as they truly are,
as well as the non-subjugation by reproach.
What is the timely turning back?
It is this: knowledge of the proper time.
... What is lack of trust in ordinary persons?
It is this: seeing the faults inherent in the qualities of the foolish.
...What is non-contempt for those who suffer?
It is this: equanimity of mind toward all sentient beings.
What is the giving of wealth to those who are suffering?
It is this: the gift of worldly material goods.
What is the non-depression of the poor?
It is this: having a mind of compassion toward others.
...What is compassion for those of immoral conduct?
It is this: the lifting of others from their transgressions and the establishment of them in ethical discipline.
...What is the state of being a beneficial thing?
It is this: the act of performing assistance for others.
What is the state of having a compassionate mind?
It is this: seeing the future suffering of sentient beings.
...What is assistance through the Dharma?
It is this: causing others to enter into the Dharma as it truly is.
...What is the relinquishing of material things?
It is this: the relinquishing of the aggregates and the bestowing of material assistance upon others.
...What is the state of not hoarding?
It is this: loathing for worldly gain and seeing the fault in guarding it.
...What is the praise of ethical discipline?
It is the realization of the fruits of ethical discipline.
What is the loathing of immorality?
It is this: the perception of the fault in immorality.
What is the unshakable service toward those who possess ethical discipline?
It is the knowledge that perceives those possessing ethical discipline as being difficult to encounter.
What is the relinquishment of all possessions?
It is this: a virtuous intention.
What is the invitation based on resolute intention?
It is the desire for the welfare and happiness of others.
What is acting according to what has been said?
It is the perfection of a virtuous intention.
...What is frequent attendance?
It is the seeking out and questioning regarding what is wholesome.
...What is the experience of joy?
It is this: the knowledge of realization and the knowledge of scripture.
...What is the knowledge of analogies?
That is to say: knowledge of analogies and knowledge of instruction.
...What is skill in former lives?
It is this: the recollection of births and the abundance of learning.
What is the state of being preceded by the roots of virtue?
It is this: having an intense aspiration for awakening and encouraging others [toward it].
...What is skill in means?
It is this: skill in confession, rejoicing, requesting [the Buddhas to teach], and the dedication of wholesome roots.

...What is the abandonment of signs (*nimittaprahāṇa*)? It is the realization that phenomena are like dreams and the discernment of their lack of substantial reality. ...What is the reversal of perception (*saṃjñāvivarta*)?
That is to say, the relinquishing of misconceptions.
...What is the characteristic of things?
It is this: the knowledge of the absence of characteristics.
What is skill in the production of discourses?
It is the thorough elucidation of phenomena as they truly are—whether wholesome or unwholesome—by means of parables and narratives.
...What is the determination of truth?
It is this: the cessation of consciousness and the non-arising of name-and-form.
...What is the realization of liberation?
It is the immovability and the unshakeability of the diamond-like samādhi.
...What is the single utterance?
It is this: the revulsion toward the abodes of the non-Buddhists and the knowledge of non-arising.
...What is the attainment of fearlessness?
It is this: the thorough realization of the Buddha-dharmas.
...What is the basis of ethical discipline?
It is this: restraint of the body and the restraint of the Prātimokṣa.
...What is the entry into meditative attainments?
It is this: detachment from the three realms.
...What is the attainment of wisdom?
It is this: both the knowledge of capability and non-perception.
...What is delighting in solitude? It is this: avoiding the faults of socializing and not abandoning wholesome qualities.
...What is contentment with little knowledge? It is this: contentment with whatever one has obtained.
... What is the clarity of the mind?
It is the suppression of the hindrances.
What is the avoidance of speculative views?
It is the avoidance of the view of apprehension.
...What is the attainment of dhāraṇī?
It is this: the unattached and thorough elucidation of phenomena exactly as they have been seen, according to reality.
...What is the entry into knowledge?
It is this: the penetration into intrinsic nature.
...the station? It is this: the station of ethical discipline.
...the state of abiding?
It is this: the state of mind.
...What is the foundation?
It is this: the foundation of faith.
...What is practice?
It is this: the practice of the path.
... what is the cause? It is this: ignorance is the cause of saṃsāra.
...What is the method? It is this: knowledge is the method for liberation.
...What is the method? It is this: the abandonment of craving.
...the door? It is this: the abandonment of faults. ...the path?
It is this: the knowledge of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self.
...What is the ground? It is this: the ground of the ten wishless states.
...What is the departure from birth?
It is this: the cutting off of birth.
...What is the stage of knowledge?
It is this: the absence of delusion.
...What is the abandonment of ignorance?
It is this: the abandonment of delusion.
...What is the foundation of knowledge? It is this: non-abiding.
... What is the *yogācārabhūmi*?
It is the cultivation of the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (*bodhipakṣikā dharmāḥ*).
...What is the sphere of activity of a bodhisattva?
It is this: the six perfections.
What is the service of holy persons?
It is this: being closely attended upon by the Buddhas.
What is the avoidance of unworthy persons?
It is the avoidance of those who belong to non-Buddhist sects and hold views based on the perception of objective existence.
...how is it described by the Tathāgatas?
That is to say: liberation through primordial wisdom (prakṛtijñāna) by abiding in the powers of a Buddha. ... What is the stage of a Buddha (buddhabhūmi)?
That is to say, it is the attainment of all wholesome qualities.
...approved by the wise?
That is to say, they are approved by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present, as well as by their disciples.
...Why is it rejected by fools? Because it is difficult for all fools to understand.
...why is it difficult for śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas to understand?
It is because of the inconceivability of the qualities of a Buddha.
...Why is this not the domain of the non-Buddhists?
Because it is false pride on the part of the practitioners.
...are they embraced by the bodhisattvas?
Namely, because they are both difficult to obtain and like a great medicine.
...followed by those who possess the ten powers?
That is to say, through the application of hardship.
...Why is it to be worshipped by the gods?
Because it brings about all forms of happiness.
...why is it worthy of being honored by Brahmā?
Because it brings about the attainment of liberation for all.
... why is it worthy of being paid homage by the Nāgas?
That is to say, it is by virtue of having completely abandoned all habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*).
...Why is it to be rejoiced in by yakṣas?
Because it serves to cut off the path to all miserable destinies.
Why is it to be praised by the kinnaras? Because it brings about the joy of liberation for all beings. Why is it to be extolled by the mahoragas?
That is to say, by virtue of the eradication of saṃsāra.
...how should it be cultivated by bodhisattvas?
Namely, by taking up that which brings about all-knowledge.
...should it be mastered by the wise?
That is to say, by means of attaining the stage of non-retrogression.
...What is unsurpassed wealth? It is that which, taking into account both the acquisition of prosperity for the realm of gods and humans and the acquisition of liberation, [constitutes such wealth].
...What is unworldly giving?
It is that which, by virtue of cutting through all afflictions, serves as their severer.
... What is the medicine for the sick?
It is this: the pacification of passion, hatred, and delusion.
What is the treasury of knowledge?
It is this: that which is based upon cultivation.
...What is the inexhaustibility of eloquence?
It is this: based upon the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are.

...the departure of sorrow? It is this: by taking up the realization that the perception of the suffering of illness is meaningless, and by taking up the thorough understanding of selflessness and suffering.
... What is the full comprehension of the triple world?
It is this: by way of understanding it as being like a dream and an illusion.
... What is the ship of the perfections?
It is this: for those who desire to attain parinirvāṇa through resolute intention, it consists in the cultivation of impermanence, suffering, and emptiness.
... for those caught in the midst of the flood of saṃsāra?
It is because it provides nourishment for nirvāṇa.
... What is fame for those who desire renown?
It is this: being a recipient of the vast Dharma.
...What is the complexion of the Buddhas?
It is this: that they have, as their basis, the mastery of bestowing the medicine of infinite virtues.
...What is the glory of the Tathāgatas?
It is this: namely, being the lord of the gift of liberation and the happiness of all virtues.
...What is the praise of those who possess the ten powers?
It is this: namely, [the praise] based upon the giver of the jewel of the Dharma, which is difficult to find.
...What are the qualities of bodhisattvas?
Namely, they consist in their being trained in the Dharma.
...What is equanimity for those who are compassionate?
It is this: having based it upon the fact that the duties and tasks to be performed by a Buddha have already been accomplished.
...What is the pacification of faults through loving-kindness? It is by virtue of its being the antidote to hostility.
...What is the breath of those belonging to the Mahāyāna?
It is this: because it brings about the fulfillment of the intentions regarding all the qualities of a Buddha.
...What is the practice of those who roar the lion’s roar? It is this: the taking up of the foremost dharma and the supreme dharma.
... what is the path to the knowledge of a Buddha?
It is this: namely, the bringing forth of all wholesome dharmas.
... What is the seal of all dharmas?
It is this: the realization that there is no further shore beyond the shoreless.
...What is the indestructibility of omniscience?
It is that which leads to the abandonment of all unwholesome states, to the gathering of all wholesome states, and to the bringing about of liberation for all sentient beings.
...What is the garden of the bodhisattvas?
It is this: namely, by means of their own happiness consisting of all joy and gladness, they bring about the happiness of all sentient beings.
...the routing of Māra’s army?
It is this: by means of seizing all powers and by means of the pacification of all afflictions.
...this knowledge belongs to those who go toward security, in that it leads to the destruction of all calamities.
... what is the meaning for those who have attained realization? It is this: having taken up the bringing about of the perfection of all dharmas.
...What is the protection for those caught in the midst of enemies?
It is that which leads to the defeat of all those who perceive [objects] and hold false views.
...What is the refutation of the non-Buddhists by means of the Dharma?
It is this: taking up the refutation of the non-Buddhists by means of the Dharma.
What is the aspect of truth regarding the grounds of self-confidence?
It is this: based on the security resulting from having thoroughly examined and re-examined all phenomena.
What is the thorough investigation of reality regarding the powers?
It is this: by means of non-erroneous application.
...What is the precursor sign of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
It is this: the bringing forth of all pure dharmas.
...What is the ornament?
It is that which, by means of bringing about the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, serves as its basis.
...What is the delight for those who desire liberation?
It is this: on account of its excellence in the beginning, middle, and end.
...What is the joy of the eldest sons?
It is this: that they receive the paternal inheritance by means of partaking in the power of the Buddha’s wealth.
...What is the fulfillment of the Buddha-knowledge?
It is, namely, by means of the protection of all pure dharmas and by means of the non-separation from the nourishment and acquisition of all pure dharmas.
Why is it not the domain of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
Because it brings about the acquisition of the vast and immeasurable qualities of a Buddha.
What is the complete purification of the mind?
It is that which leads to the abandonment of all stains.
...What is the purification of the body? It is this: by virtue of the pacification of all ailments. ...What is the perfection of the gateways to liberation?
That is to say, it is based upon the contemplation of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, selflessness, and peace.
...What is non-affliction with regard to passion?
It is this: taking up that which brings about the state of the deathless.
...What is the removal of fault?
It is this: having taken up the sustenance of great loving-kindness.
...is it not the ground of delusion?
Because it takes as its basis the illumination of the true nature of phenomena.
...What is the source of cognition?
It is this: based upon the arising of all mundane and supramundane knowledge of the body.
... what is the arising of knowledge?
It is this: by virtue of removing all improper mental attention.
...What is the abandonment of ignorance?
It is that which leads to the departure from all improper mental attention.
...What is the satisfaction of those for whom liberation is the essence?
It is this: by virtue of attaining the noble majesty.
...What is the contentment of those for whom meditative concentration is the essence?
It is this: by virtue of bringing about one-pointedness of mind toward all forms of happiness.
...What is the eye for those who desire to see?
It is this: based on the state of "I see."
...What is the supernormal power of those who wish to perform transformations?
It is this: by virtue of being unobstructed and by virtue of the quality of being desirable.
...What is the supernormal power (*ṛddhi*) of those who desire to overcome others?
It is this: by virtue of the non-obstruction of knowledge regarding the conceptualization of all phenomena.
... What is the dhāraṇī for those who seek to hear the meaning?
It is this: by means of the equality of all phenomena with nirvāṇa.
What is the non-forgetfulness of mindfulness?
It is that which, based on the natural subsiding of the objective referent of nirvāṇa.
...What is the empowerment of the Buddhas?
It is this: by virtue of their infinite capacity for bringing forth.
...What is the skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) of the Protectors?
It is this: namely, by virtue of leading [beings] to all happiness and security.
...What is subtle? It is this: based upon the tranquility of taking nirvāṇa as one's object.
...difficult to understand? Because it is characterized by the nature of being difficult to comprehend as suffering.
...Why is it difficult for those who are not diligent to understand?
It is because it has never been attained before.
...What is the transformation of syllables?
It is that which consists in the non-apprehension of all speech and discourse.
...Why is it difficult to understand by means of sound?
Because all phenomena are inconceivable.
...is it unknown to the wise?
It is so because it possesses the quality of being a jewel of great value.
...What is knowledge through pleasant experiences? It is that which arises from the absence of attachment to honor.
...awakened by those with few desires?
That is to say, by virtue of their lack of attachment to honor.
...by those who have grasped [the teaching] and initiated their vigor?
It is this: by virtue of not laying down the burden.
...is it upheld by those possessed of mindfulness?
It is so because of the non-perishing of what has been done.
...What is the exhaustion of suffering? It is this: based on the cessation of passion, hatred, and delusion.
...What is the non-arising of all phenomena?
It is this: based upon the cessation of all consciousnesses.
...the teaching on the single principle.
That is to say: "All phenomena of all states of existence, destinies, deaths, births, and bases are like a dream," based on the non-arising of all phenomena.
This should be seen as the explanation of these three hundred terms.
This, young man, is called the samādhi named "The Manifestation of the Equality of the Essential Nature of All Phenomena."
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter of the *Śrīsamādhirāja*.
(Vaidya 303) Chapter 40: The Entrustment.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
For the qualities of a Buddha are vast, and the method taught is vast;
having taught the vast Dharma, one obtains vast virtues.
Just as space is vast, such is the characteristic of phenomena;
because the jewels therein are vast, it is therefore called Vaipulya.
The conduct of sentient beings is vast, and it is taught as vast for them;
because its arrival is vast, it is therefore called "Vaipulya" (the Extensive).

Furthermore, while this Dharma discourse titled "The Exposition of the Samādhi Manifesting the Equality of the Essential Nature of All Phenomena" was being taught, immeasurable beings resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
and immeasurable beings became irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
and the thought of individual awakening arose in immeasurable beings.
The minds of immeasurable beings were set upon the realization of the fruit of arhatship;
and this trichiliocosm, the great trichiliocosm world-system, shook, trembled, and quaked; it moved, vibrated, and shook violently in six ways.
It was shaken, it was shaken violently,
it was shaken all over;
it was stirred, it was stirred violently, it was stirred all over.
It resounded, it resonated, it vibrated;
it thundered, it roared, it reverberated.
The eastern direction sank down while the western direction rose up.
The western direction sinks and the eastern direction rises;
the northern direction rises and the southern direction sinks;
the northern direction sinks and the southern direction rises.
It sank down at the edges and rose up in the center;
it sank down in the center and rose up at the edges;
and an immeasurable radiance appeared in the world.
And a great rain of divine fragrances fell;
the deities released a vast rain of divine flowers,
and hundreds of thousands of divine musical instruments resounded in the sky above.
And they spoke these words:
"Well-gained are the gains of those beings who shall hear this Dharma-discourse on the entrance into great compassion.
Those beings who shall repeatedly hear this Samādhi of the Manifestation of the Equality of the Essential Nature of All Dharmas will have attended upon many Buddhas."

And having heard it, they will write it down, take it up, retain it, master it, cultivate it through the meditation on non-contention (araṇā), practice it extensively, and reveal it in detail to others.
They will become worthy recipients of offerings for all sentient beings.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, take up this Dharma-discourse; retain it, recite it, master it, and reveal it in detail to others.
Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma-discourse?”
"And how should I uphold it?
The Blessed One said: "Ānanda, uphold this sūtra as 'The Descent of Great Compassion.
Uphold it as the samādhi called 'The Manifestation of the Equality of All Dharmas.'"
Ānanda said: "I have grasped this Dharma discourse, Blessed One."
The Blessed One spoke thus. The youth Candraprabha, the venerable Ānanda, those four assemblies— monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—
and many sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, as well as the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, were delighted by the Blessed One’s words.
They rejoiced in what was spoken.

Thus ends the fortieth chapter, titled "The King of Samādhis," from the Mahāyāna sūtra *The Manifestation of the Equality of the Essential Nature of All Phenomena*, as obtained from the noble *Samādhi*.
